**Finding: deviation (high severity) — Section 6.1 Exclusivity**

Contrary to the planner's "likely absent" hint, the document does contain a non-compete binding our party. The keyword sweep for "compet" returned nothing because the covenant is framed as "Exclusivity" and worded around "any project similar to the Site."

**What I found**

- **p0037 (§6.1)** — restricts the *Company* from participating in any internet project similar to the Site with respect to Deerskin Products "or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including... companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled)."
- **p0042 (§6.3)** — the mirror-image restriction on HDI (two years post-term). This binds the vendor and benefits us, so I did not flag it.

**Why it fails the fallback**

1. **Scope not limited to a named competing product** — "substantially similar" products and "companies similar to" the named retailers is an elastic, open-ended class.
2. **No internal-development or acquisition carve-out** — the only carve-outs are §6.2 (closeouts) and the §1.1 exclusions (closeouts, Joan Cook Catalog). An acquisition of, or internal build of, a leather apparel web business would breach.
3. **12-month cap not met in substance** — §4.1 (p0024) makes the one-year term automatically renew on each anniversary, so a "term-only" covenant can run indefinitely.

It stays out of walk-away territory because there is no post-term tail on us and the scope is at least anchored to a defined product category rather than "any competing business."

**Proposal — fallback rather than preferred.** Preferred would be deletion, but HDI builds and hosts the site, takes the exclusive "Deerskin" brand right, and accepts a *longer* reciprocal covenant in §6.3, so the bargain plausibly needs protection and deletion would be disproportionate. The redline (validated ok:true) narrows scope to Deerskin Products, caps the covenant at twelve months from the Effective Date, and adds a carve-out for other products, internal development, and acquisitions — leaving HDI's brand exclusivity and §6.3 untouched.
